evaluation.ideal_answer: A Binary Search Tree is a data structure where each node has at most two children and each node represents a value. For any given node, all elements in its left subtree are less than the node, and all elements in its right subtree are greater, which facilitates efficient search, insertion, and deletion operations with an average time complexity of O(log n). This makes BSTs crucial in practice for applications requiring quick data retrieval and manipulation, such as database indexing.
